sections.h2: What should anyone selling a Michigan home understand first?
sections.html:
Nearly three of every four Michigan housing units are lived in by their owners: 73.2% for 2020 to 2024, per Census QuickFacts. The same table lists $231,600 as the middle owner-occupied home value, $1,129 for gross rent, 4,076,369 households, and a mid-2025 population estimate of 10,127,884.

The state has two peninsulas, the more populated Lower Peninsula and the heavily forested Upper Peninsula, joined across the Straits of Mackinac. Lansing is the capital, Detroit is the most populous city, and Wayne is the largest county. Michigan borders four of the five Great Lakes and has the longest freshwater coastline of any U.S. political subdivision, 3,288 miles, per Wikipedia.

The sections below cover rules that apply in every Michigan county. The local pages on this site add the details of individual offices.

sections.h2: Which local offices handle what in Michigan?
sections.html:
Michigan has 83 counties. Townships are divisions of counties, and cities, villages, and state universities hold home rule powers of differing degrees. A house sale touches several offices at once, and the tasks split roughly as follows.

  • City or township assessor: receives the principal residence exemption affidavit and rescission form, and decides whether a transfer uncaps taxable value.
  • County treasurer: collects the state real estate transfer tax on a recorded sale.
  • Register of deeds, one per county: records the deed, receives redemption payments after a foreclosure sale, and notifies the local tax collecting unit of a recorded transfer (MCL 211.7cc(17)).
  • District court: hears landlord-tenant summary proceedings.
  • Probate court: handles estates, and the small estate affidavit form PC 598 is available only where no real property is in the estate.

Treasury's property tax page groups the state's programs into categories that include deferment, forfeiture and foreclosure, exemptions, the Homestead Property Tax Credit, veterans and military personnel, and changes in ownership. A seller facing delinquent tax should start there and then call the county treasurer.

sections.h2: Which Michigan rules apply in every county?
sections.html:

sections.h2: How long does a Michigan homeowner have to redeem after a foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
It depends on the property type and the mortgage balance. MCL 600.3240 sets these periods for foreclosure by advertisement.

  • Commercial, industrial, or multifamily property above 4 units: 6 months from the sale date.
  • Residential property of up to 4 units, where the amount claimed at the notice date is more than 66-2/3% of the original debt: 6 months.
  • Residential property of up to 4 units that is abandoned under the statute's test: 1 month, or 30 days under a separate abandonment section.
  • Agricultural property: 1 year, with a presumption tied to a filed federal Schedule F and a recorded affidavit.
  • Anything else: 1 year.

To redeem, the owner or a person with a recorded interest pays the sale bid, interest from the sale date at the mortgage rate, the sheriff's fee the purchaser paid, and a $5 custody fee if paid to the register of deeds. The purchaser records an affidavit stating the exact amount. A register of deeds in a county with a population between 750,000 and 1,500,000 will compute the figure on request for no more than $50.

sections.h2: Which tax comes due when a Michigan deed is delivered?
sections.html:
The state real estate transfer tax falls on the grantor (MCL 207.523). The money goes to the treasurer of the county that holds the parcel, no later than 15 days after the instrument is handed over. The tax reaches deeds given for consideration, contracts of sale or exchange, and transfers of a controlling interest in an entity whose assets are at least 90% real property. A grantor who later decides an exemption fit can ask Treasury for a refund. Your closing agent can quote the rate and say which exemptions suit your sale.

On the property tax side, a sale is a transfer of ownership that normally uncaps taxable value for the buyer in the following calendar year, with a list of exempt transfers in MCL 211.27a(7), according to Treasury. The seller's own filing is the rescission of the principal residence exemption, which the closing agent is supposed to supply forms for.

sections.h2: What are the main routes to selling a house in Michigan?
sections.html:
Most Michigan sales fall into a handful of situations, and each has its own paperwork. Heirs of a house go through the probate court, since the small estate affidavit cannot cover real property. An owner behind on a mortgage works against the redemption clock described above. An owner with a tenant works within the summary proceedings schedule, and the security deposit has to be passed to the buyer with notice to the tenant (MCL 554.614).

A seller who owns through a lady bird deed, trust, or land contract needs to read the ownership rules for the principal residence exemption, since Treasury lists who counts as an owner. Michigan Treasury also publishes information on tax forfeiture, foreclosure, and auction for owners who let property taxes go unpaid.

  • Inherited house: start at the probate court serving the decedent's last residence.
  • Behind on the mortgage: the certificate of sale states the redemption deadline.
  • Rented house: serve the right notice and keep the deposit paperwork.
  • Delinquent taxes: request a payoff figure, and ask about deferment, from the treasurer.

sections.h2: How should I use the city and county guides on this site?
sections.html: Begin with the page for the house's county, then add the city or township page if one exists. County offices set their own hours, fees, and recording steps, while the statutes above supply only the outer limits. The statewide pages on property tax, probate, foreclosure, the principal residence exemption, eviction, and lady bird deeds cover the topics each county page assumes you know.

faqs.q: How many counties make up Michigan?
faqs.a: Michigan has 83 counties. Townships are administrative divisions of a county, and cities, villages, and state universities hold home rule powers to varying degrees, according to the state's general description.

faqs.q: Who bears the state transfer tax on a Michigan sale?
faqs.a: The grantor, under MCL 207.523. A buyer who pays it on the grantor's behalf can also request a refund when an exemption applied.

faqs.q: What does the Census report for typical Michigan home values?
faqs.a: $231,600 for 2020 to 2024, per the Census QuickFacts table for Michigan. The same table shows 73.2% of housing units occupied by their owners.

faqs.q: Can an heir use the small estate affidavit to sell a house?
faqs.a: No. Court form PC 598 requires that no real property be included in the decedent's estate, so a house needs a court proceeding with a personal representative.

faqs.q: When does a foreclosure sale become final for the owner?
faqs.a: Under MCL 600.3240 the redemption period after the sale is 6 months for a residential mortgage of up to 4 units when more than 66-2/3% of the original debt is claimed, and 1 year for property that fits none of the shorter categories.
